name: Support Chat
description:
A small company support portal running at http://webapp:80. Target base URL inside the challenge network: BASE=http://webapp:80
If testing from host: BASE=http://localhost:8080

Goal: Reach /flag (it returns 403 unless you have the right privileges).

What you can discover:
- Register/login flows exist; a chat feature is available after login (/dashboard → POST to /chat).
- An internal viewer periodically checks a privileged page related to chat moderation.
- Messages appear to be rendered rather than treated as plain text.
- There is a simple endpoint that stores and later displays arbitrary data submitted as a parameter.

Suggested approach (not exhaustive):
1) Register and keep a session cookie jar.
   curl -i -c jar -b jar -X POST "$BASE/register" \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
        --data 'username=u1&password=p1'

2) Post a crafted message to the chat. Consider whether a background viewer might process it and how you could confirm that.
   # Fill in the message content yourself
   curl -i -c jar -b jar -X POST "$BASE/chat" \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
        --data-urlencode 'msg=YOUR_MESSAGE_HERE'

3) Check the endpoint that records arbitrary data to verify that your message had the intended side effect.
   curl -i "$BASE/leak"

4) Once you obtain whatever client-side state is required, replay a request to /flag with it.
   # Replace the placeholder header with the appropriate value once you discover it
   curl -i -H 'Cookie: NAME=VALUE' "$BASE/flag"

Utilities:
- Health check: /health
- Hints page: /hint
- Data viewer: /leak
